# Knowledge Article

`customer_support.obj.core.knowledge_article` · v1.0.0 · **draft** · scope **core**

> A durable answer, written once, reachable without a human. Distinct from a Macro (which is an agent's shortcut, sent BY a person) and from a Resolution (which is what made one customer's problem stop). An article is a standing claim about how the product behaves, addressed to a stranger, and it keeps making that claim long after the product stopped behaving that way. Its value is not that it exists, is well written, or is recently edited — it is that a specific person with a specific question found it and did not then need us. Everything measurable about the first three is easy to collect and nearly worthless; the fourth is the only one that matters and is almost never instrumented.


Also called: `KB Article`, `Help Center Article`, `Doc`, `Support Article`, `Solution Article`

## Constraints

- **`ka.no_reuse_after_unverified_release`** May not be sent as an authoritative answer when the documented area has shipped a change since last_verified_at.
- **`ka.gated_content_is_not_a_public_answer`** An entitled_only or logged_in article may not be offered to a requester who cannot reach it, nor counted as coverage for them.
- **`ka.view_never_counts_as_deflection`** A view, a click or a dwell time may never be recorded as a deflected contact.
- **`ka.no_customer_data_in_public_content`** Public articles may not contain account names, ticket excerpts or reproduction data taken from a real case.
- **`ka.locale_variant_verified_separately`** A translated variant does not inherit the source article's verification. It carries its own, or it is unverified. _(soft)_
- **`ka.agent_only_excluded_from_deflection`** audience = agent_only content may not appear in customer-facing deflection coverage.


## Business rules

- **`ka.no_publish_without_named_owner`** An article may not be published without a named owner. "Team owned" does not satisfy this — a team cannot be asked whether something is still true.
- **`ka.edit_must_not_advance_verification`** An edit must never advance last_verified_at. Verification is a separate act against a named product version. Collapsing the two makes every article permanently fresh and permanently unchecked, and it is the default behaviour of most knowledge bases.

- **`ka.view_is_not_deflection`** A view may not be counted as a deflection. Deflection may only be claimed when no contact from that person on that intent followed inside the window. Counting views is how a support org reports rising deflection while its ticket volume also rises.

- **`ka.overdue_promised_update_blocks_reuse`** An article with an overdue promised update must be flagged before an agent or an AI answer reuses it.
- **`ka.orphan_is_not_coverage`** An article nothing links to must be excluded from coverage counts. It is inventory, not coverage.
- **`ka.gated_article_is_not_self_service`** An article behind an entitlement the requester does not hold may not be offered as a self-service answer or counted as available coverage for that requester.

- **`ka.no_customer_identifiers_in_public_articles`** Articles drafted from a ticket must not carry account names, ticket bodies or reproduction data. This is the most frequent real incident caused by knowledge authoring, and it is caused by the correct instinct of writing from a real case.

## Outputs

- **`answer_confidence_bp`** How sure we are this article is currently correct. Must fall on release activity, not only on age. → L4.reasoning_unit
- **`send_ready`** Whether an agent or AI answer may reuse this right now. False on overdue maintenance or a post-verification release. → L5.communication_planning, L5.2.channel_planner
- **`deflection_candidate`** Whether this could plausibly answer the incoming intent WITHOUT a human. Gated content is never a candidate. → L4.decision_maker
- **`decay_risk_bp`** Predicted probability the article is already wrong. Drives the verification queue order. → L4.reasoning_unit, L6.learning_unit
- **`coverage_gap_signal`** Demand observed against this topic that the article did not satisfy. Feeds content_gap_analysis. → L4.reasoning_unit
- **`verification_due`** A human must re-check the claim against the shipping product. → L5.execution_planning

## Actions

- **Re-verify against the shipping product** (human) — Sets last_verified_at AND verified_against_version. Either one alone is theatre.
- **Assign a named owner** (human) — Converts ownership_state away from unowned. A team is not an owner.
- **Rewrite the title and terms in customer language** (human) — The highest-yield and least-glamorous fix. Most 'content gaps' are vocabulary gaps in disguise.
- **Add synonyms harvested from search logs** (agent) — Harvested, never invented — the people who can invent them already know the answer and therefore use the wrong words.
- **Link this article from the matching macro** (agent) — Keeps the agent path and the customer path pointing at one source of truth. When they diverge, the macro wins and the article rots.
- **Draft an article from a repeated resolution** (agent) — Trigger on the second occurrence, not the first. Drafting from one case produces an article about one customer.
- **Retire and redirect** (human) — Redirect, never delete. A deleted article's inbound links fail silently and the traffic simply disappears from the numbers.


## Evidence

- **telemetry** · 9500 bp — Release and version data for the documented surface. The only source that can prove an article WRONG rather than merely old.
- **ticket** · 8500 bp — A contact filed minutes after a view. A receipt that the article failed, and the strongest negative evidence there is.
- **help_center** · 8000 bp — Search and view logs. Tells you what was asked, which nothing else does.
- **knowledge_base** · 6000 bp — Edit history and metadata. Proves the file changed. Says nothing about whether the claim is true — this is the source most often mistaken for proof.
- **email** · 5000 bp — An agent chose to paste this link. A quiet, unprompted quality vote, and more honest than a survey.
- **survey** · 4000 bp — Thumbs and comments. Bimodal and thin. Useful as a pointer, never as a verdict, and its silence means nothing at all.
- **derived** · 3500 bp — Graph degree and inferred decay. Corroborating only — it orders the queue, it does not decide anything.
- **manual_entry** · 3000 bp — Somebody ticked reviewed. Worth something only when accompanied by a version; without one it is a date.


## Metrics

- **article_to_ticket_rate** (percent) — Views followed by a contact from the same person on the same intent. The number this object exists to produce, and currently uncomputable.
- **zero_result_query_rate** (percent) — Share of help-centre searches returning nothing. The cheapest proxy for what is asked and uncovered.
- **verified_coverage_of_top_intents** (percent) — Top intents by volume with a VERIFIED article. Coverage measured against demand, not against the catalogue — the denominator is the whole point.
- **median_days_since_verification** (days) — Across published articles. Use the median, not the mean: a handful of hot articles updated weekly hides a long tail nobody has read since launch.
- **agent_link_rate** (percent) — Share of replies on a covered intent that link the article rather than rewriting it. A quality signal that costs nothing to collect.
- **orphan_article_share** (percent) — Published articles with zero inbound links. Computable today from graph degree.
- **time_to_correct** (hours) — From a contradiction being detected to the article being corrected. The metric that separates a knowledge base from an archive.
- **deflection_attributed** (count) — Retained because it is what gets reported. Flagged because it is the most gamed number in support — it improves when help is harder to find.


## Examples

- **"Resetting your API key" — 4k views/month, thumbs never used, ticket volume on the same intent flat and high** — The canonical silent failure. Every reported number looks healthy. It is being found, read, and failed, and no field currently on the object can say so.
- **Migration guide edited nine days ago, UI redesigned eleven months ago** — Fresh and wrong. last_edited_at is recent, last_verified_at is absent, verified_against_version is null. Passes every freshness audit ever run.
- **Accurate billing article at search position four for its own primary question** — findability = weakly_findable. Operationally identical to not existing. The fix is synonyms and a title rewrite, not a new article — and the content-gap report will recommend a new article.
- **Known-issue notice for a bug fixed two releases ago, still indexed, still ranked first** — Now actively harmful: it tells customers a resolved problem is unresolved and generates contacts on its own. Retire and redirect; deleting it 404s the inbound links and the traffic vanishes from the numbers instead of being explained.
- **Detailed SSO troubleshooting guide behind entitled_only visibility** — findability = gated. Cannot deflect a pre-login contact, however good it is, and every coverage dashboard counts it. The fix is commercial, not editorial.
- **Article written from one enterprise ticket, published with the account's hostname in the example** — Two failures at once: a data-exposure incident, and an article scoped to a single customer's configuration that will mislead everyone else.

## Metadata

owner **Customer Support** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **provisional** · completeness **partial**


> Five of thirteen patterns are executable, and all five read graph degree or a maintenance commitment — the only two things in today's substrate that touch a document at all. The eight needs_signal entries are, between them, the entire argument for a support_v1 pack: knowledge.viewed_at joined to ticket_created is the highest-value single ask in this brain, and both halves are already collected everywhere and joined nowhere.
Signal names not yet in vocabulary planned_substrate and proposed by this object: knowledge.viewed_at, knowledge.view_count_30d, knowledge.owner_id, search.query_text, search.result_count, product.released_at, product.surface_version, knowledge_feedback_submitted (obs_kind), article_link_rate (baseline). leaver_confirmed is reused from the Admin planned list rather than duplicated — one emitter, two domains.
One executable pattern was considered and deliberately NOT authored: followup_sent plus thread.ball_in_court = us as a proxy for article-to-ticket conversion. It is grammatical and it would have made the headline metric look covered while measuring something else. That is structurally the same error as binding "SLA breach imminent" to unanswered_email, which the domain header names as the failure this whole architecture exists to prevent.
ka.traffic_without_feedback is set at 3500 on purpose and should be defended in review. Its job is to cap confidence, not to assert anything. Raising it turns "we are not watching" into "it is working", which is the precise mistake this object was written about.
